activities.anchor: Every long-horizon policy question funnels into one parameter
activities.caption: call the magnitude — a century of discounting
activities.name: eepDiscountEstimate

config.prompt: Present value = future amount ÷ (1 + r)^t. At a 3% discount rate, what is $100 of climate damage in the year 2125 worth today?
config.why: 100 ÷ 1.03¹⁰⁰ ≈ $5 — a century of care discounted to the price of a sandwich. At Stern's 1% ethical rate the same damage is worth ≈ $37, seven times more.
config.context: Nothing else in the calculation moves — only the rate, which is a philosophical answer wearing a parameter's clothing.

activities.anchor: The Stern–Nordhaus dispute is exactly this
activities.caption: fill the blanks — two rates, two centuries
activities.name: eepSternCloze

config.text: Stern chose a near-zero %%0%% time preference — the year of your birth is no reason to count for less — and got aggressive immediate action. Nordhaus's DICE model used market-observed rates and got gradual ramping, with an SCC of tens rather than hundreds of dollars. The conclusions that %%1%% the choice: aggressive near-term action, once uncertainty, tipping risks and the option value of not locking in infrastructure are counted.
config.hint: One side called it an ethical question; the other called it a market observation. Neither is an arithmetic error.

activities.anchor: The flagship test was American acid rain
activities.caption: rebuild the cap-and-trade learning curve
activities.name: eepETSOrder

config.prompt: From proof-of-concept to meaningful price — put the cap-and-trade story in order:
items: 1990: the Clean Air Act's Title IV caps SO₂ and lets utilities trade allowances
Emissions halve through the 1990s at a fraction of the predicted cost
The EU ETS over-allocates: the price collapses to under €5 by 2017
The institutional fix: a market stability reserve tightens supply
Prices climb past €80–100 by 2022–23 — finally in the range economists consider meaningful
config.why: The proof-of-concept made the EU ETS possible; over-allocation taught the design lesson that scarcity, not existence, is what signals.

activities.anchor: deployment subsidies in Germany and China
activities.caption: which curve is Wright's law?
activities.name: eepWrightTrace

config.prompt: Subsidies drive the doublings; learning cuts the cost. If each production doubling cuts module cost by about a fifth, which curve shows cost (indexed to 1) against doublings?
config.why: 0.8¹⁰ ≈ 0.11 — and the real decline since 1976 was ~99.9%. The same arithmetic now runs batteries, and is attempting it for hydrogen and DAC.

activities.anchor: Three tests decide whether a credit is real
activities.caption: pair each integrity test with its way of failing
activities.name: eepOffsetMatch

config.prompt: The offset integrity tests — pair each with its failure mode:

pairs.right: the forest was never under threat — the protection was happening regardless
a tree burns; a tonne avoided this year does not bank against future emissions
protect one forest, and the logging moves next door
the baseline games the 2023 investigations caught in forest programmes

config.why: The reform direction is structural: conservative jurisdiction-scale baselines, reversal-risk buffers, and a hard split between compensation claims and real residual emissions.

activities.anchor: The distributional design, not the price, decides survival
activities.caption: you are pricing carbon — where does the money go?
activities.name: eepRevenueBranch

config.root: A country is about to charge for carbon in motor fuels. The economics is ready; the politics is the open question.

choices.label: Back to citizens as equal per-capita dividends
choices.feedback: The bottom deciles become net winners in most analyses.

choices.label: Into the treasury, unmarked
choices.feedback: The cost shows at the pump; the benefit shows nowhere.

choices.label: Into exemptions for the industries that lobby hardest
choices.feedback: Windfall profits for the few, visible cost for the many.

dividends.text: British Columbia has run its revenue-neutral scheme since 2008 with public support — it pays its own way publicly.

jaunes.text: France, 2018: no visible recycling on top of rural cost of living — the gilets jaunes detonated, and the increase was withdrawn.

carveouts.text: Free allocation was the EU ETS's early wound: windfall profits with no visible public return — the least durable of the three.

config.why: The instruments that work are the ones that pay their own way publicly — fuel charges are regressive unless revenues are returned.

activities.anchor: The treaty history is a sequence of designs tested against that structure
activities.caption: scrub the treaty record
activities.name: eepTreatyTimeline

events.title: Kyoto
events.text: Top-down binding targets for developed nations only — the US never ratifies, Canada quits, and global emissions rise.

events.title: Paris
events.text: The inversion: no binding targets, universal participation, nationally determined contributions, five-yearly stocktake and ratchet.

events.title: Finance catches up (barely)
events.text: The $100 billion/year promise is first met (per OECD), and the loss-and-damage fund is agreed.

events.title: First global stocktake
events.text: The honest verdict: current pledges land near ~2.5–2.9 °C — well short of 1.5–2 °C, needing roughly a doubling of ambition this decade.

activities.caption: two game boards — drag from dilemma to club
activities.name: eepClubCompare

config.prompt: The international endgame's two game boards:

before.label: prisoner's dilemma
before.text: Every nation gains from others' cuts whether or not it cuts itself — defect pays, and Kyoto's top-down binding targets died of it.

after.label: climate club
after.text: Members charge carbon internally, border adjustments press outsiders, technology benefits are shared among members — joining pays, and becomes the dominant strategy.

config.why: Nordhaus's proposal, endorsed for study by the G7 in 2022, is the first in which membership is a dominant strategy rather than a sacrifice.
